Office-based, five days a week Type: Full time, permanent Salary: £35,000 to £38,000 depending on experience Experience level: 1 to 3 years About Vatix Vatix builds software that helps organisations run safer, better operations. Our platform is used to capture what is happening on the front line, route it to the right people, track follow-up actions through to completion, verify standards through audits and inspections, and report on all of it in one place. Alongside the platform, we provide lone worker safety, including our own SafePro alarm device, a mobile safety app, and 24/7 monitoring by a BS 8484 accredited alarm receiving centre. Our products are used across healthcare, manufacturing, logistics, construction, education, social care and the public sector, by organisations including Intel, Siemens, the NHS, the University of Oxford and Wren Kitchens. We are profitable, independently owned and growing. Our commercial team is based in central London and our engineering and product team is in Kraków. About the opportunity We are looking for a Technical Support Specialist to join our customer support team. You will be the person our customers come to when something is not working, when they need help configuring the platform, or when they are setting up and deploying our safety devices. The variety is the appeal here. In a single day you might investigate a software issue in our web app, walk an administrator through configuring a reporting form, help a customer troubleshoot connectivity on an alarm device, and work with an engineer to get a bug diagnosed and fixed. You will be close to both the product and the customer, which is the fastest way to learn a SaaS business properly. Ultimately, you will be someone our customers trust. They will rely on you for timely, accurate answers and for clear explanations of technical detail. If you enjoy solving problems for people and you like getting to the bottom of things, we would like to meet you. What you will be doing Acting as the first point of contact for customers by phone, email and chat Diagnosing and troubleshooting technical issues across our web platform, mobile apps and safety devices Helping customers configure the platform to fit how they work, including reporting forms, audit templates, user permissions and notifications Setting up, configuring and dispatching safety alarm devices, and processing new device orders Talking customers through resolution step by step, and confirming afterwards that everything is working as it should Tracking every issue through to resolution within our agreed response and resolution times, and keeping HubSpot up to date with actions and next steps Escalating unresolved issues to the right internal team with a clear, well-documented handover, and staying the owner of the customer relationship until it is closed Prioritising and managing multiple open issues at once without losing track of any of them Using and improving our internal knowledge base, and writing help centre content so customers can self-serve Supporting the Customer Success team with onboarding, configuration and technical questions Spotting patterns in the issues you see and feeding them back to product and engineering What we are looking for Essential 1 to 3 years in a customer-facing support role, including phone and email support Experience supporting a software, SaaS or technical product, so you are comfortable with how software behaves and where things tend to break A good working understanding of computer systems, mobile devices and connected hardware The ability to diagnose and troubleshoot technical issues methodically rather than by guesswork Excellent written and verbal communication, and the ability to explain something technical to someone who is not technical Highly organised and conscientious, with strong attention to detail Comfortable working autonomously and taking full ownership of the issues assigned to you Curious, with a habit of looking for better ways of doing things Happy to speak up, give and receive candid feedback, and engage in constructive debate Nice to have Experience with HubSpot, particularly Service Hub, ticketing or knowledge base Experience with other help desk or ticketing tools such as Zendesk, Intercom, Freshdesk or Jira Exposure to IoT, connected devices, mobile app support or API troubleshooting Experience in health and safety, compliance, healthcare or another regulated environment Experience writing customer-facing documentation or help centre content You do not need to tick every box. If you are strong on problem solving, communication and ownership, and you have worked with a technical product, we want to hear from you. Why this role is worth having You will learn the whole product, not one corner of it. Support is the fastest route to genuine product depth, and our people use it as a springboard into customer success, implementation, product and revenue operations Real ownership from early on. This is a small, capable team and there is no layer of process between you and the customer Direct access to the engineers who build the product, not a ticket queue into the void You will see how a profitable, independently owned software company actually operates Life at Vatix 25 days of annual leave, plus bank holidays Pension plan Comprehensive private health insurance with Vitality benefits Regular training and a personal development budget The latest equipment and tools provided Complimentary fresh fruit and cereals, and a range of drinks including juice, tea, coffee and soft drinks A bright, well-equipped office in Southwark, a few minutes from Borough, London Bridge and Southwark stations How to apply Apply through LinkedIn with your CV and a short note on why this role interests you. We review applications as they arrive and aim to come back to everyone. Our process is: Introductory call with the hiring manager (30 minutes) Practical exercise reflecting the real work of the role Final interview with the team Vatix is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from everyone and are happy to make reasonable adjustments at any stage of the process. Let us know what you need.

review_candidates.title: Data Operations DevOps Engineer
review_candidates.description: This role is based in Cheshire, UK. At the SKAO we are coordinating a global effort to deliver one of the largest science facilities on the planet. The SKAO telescopes will be next-generation instruments that will help to answer key questions in astrophysics, drive technological innovation and support human capital development. More than a dozen partner countries and over a thousand scientists and engineers around the world are already on board, making the SKA project an international collaboration like no other, and one of the most ambitious science and engineering endeavours of the 21st century. Headquartered in the UK, with telescope sites in Australia and South Africa, the SKAO will be one observatory operating two telescopes, an endeavour spanning three continents. Multinational by design, in early 2021 the SKAO became an intergovernmental organisation, one of only a select handful of science infrastructures to do so worldwide. Our Global HQ is located near the buzzing city of Manchester at the historic Jodrell Bank Observatory, a UNESCO World Heritage site located in the Cheshire countryside. It is home to a rapidly expanding international team of more than a hundred, working in a highly collaborative and inclusive way, in coordination with SKAO teams in Australia and South Africa as part of a global astronomy and engineering community. Being part of Team SKA means contributing to something extraordinary: a uniquely exciting project to advance human knowledge that will last for decades. In return, we offer a diverse multicultural working environment, 30 days annual leave plus public holidays, a generous pension scheme, visa and support with relocation (if applicable), regular social events, a family-friendly environment and much more. Come and join us! At SKAO we are coordinating a global effort to deliver one of the largest science facilities on the planet. SKAO telescopes will be next-generation instruments that will help to answer key questions in astrophysics, drive technological innovation and support human capital development. More than a dozen partner countries and over a thousand scientists and engineers around the world are already on board, making the SKA project an international collaboration like no other, and one of the most ambitious science and engineering endeavours of the 21st century. Headquartered in the UK, with telescope sites in Australia and South Africa, SKAO will be one observatory operating two telescopes, an undertaking spanning three continents. Multinational by design, in early 2021 SKAO became an intergovernmental organisation, one of only a select handful of science infrastructures to do so worldwide. Our Global HQ is located near the buzzing city of Manchester at the historic Jodrell Bank Observatory, a UNESCO World Heritage site located in the Cheshire countryside. It is home to a rapidly expanding international team of more than a hundred, working in a highly collaborative and inclusive way, in coordination with SKAO teams in Australia and South Africa as part of a global astronomy and engineering community. Being part of Team SKA means contributing to something extraordinary: a uniquely exciting project to advance human knowledge that will last for decades. In return, we offer a diverse multicultural working environment, 30 days annual leave plus public holidays, a generous pension scheme, visa and support with relocation (if applicable), regular social events, a family-friendly environment and much more. Come and join us! This is an ideal role for a software, DevOps, or data engineer with a familiarity of scientific research settings who is keen to contribute to the development of the global network of data centres that will allow scientists to make scientific discoveries from the vast data products generated by the SKA telescopes. The Role The SKAO Data Operations group is looking to employ a talented and driven DevOps engineer to join our team based in the SKAO Global Headquarters located at Jodrell Bank in the UK. With the SKA now in construction, the development of the global network of data centres - the SKA Regional Centre Network (SRCNet) - to support the operations of the SKA has entered an exciting phase. SRCNet is crucial to the success of the SKA. The observatory’s output data products will be too large for astronomers to download and process locally; scientists will rely on the SRCNet to make new scientific discoveries. In addition to efficiently storing and managing the Exabyte-scale archive of data products globally, the SRCNet will provide tools and services for astronomers to discover, visualise and process the SKA telescope data products, promoting the principles of open science and reproducibility of results. In order to support our delivery of the SRCNet, we are looking for someone with experience in operating production web services in a cloud ecosystem. This includes a good understanding of programming languages and frameworks commonly used in web service development, as well as the containerisation and orchestration technologies that enable us to manage, maintain and further develop these services. Complementing these, a background in scientific research is desirable, but not required. Due to the global nature of the SRCNet development effort, with multiple stakeholders and developers distributed globally, the successful candidate will possess strong organisational and communication skills, with a drive to collaborate with partner organisations and people to excel in this role. SKAO is committed to providing an inclusive and flexible working environment, meeting the requests of our colleagues whilst also fulfilling the needs and objectives of the Observatory. There are expected to be occasions where this role requires the post holder to work across different time zones and travel nationally and internationally as required (e.g. ~2-4 times a year). In line with SKAO policy, flexible working hours will be supported in agreement with the line manager. Key Responsibilities, Accountabilities and Duties Effectively work within the software engineering team based at SKAO HQ, and represent the SKAO within the SRCNet Operations Group; communicating issues affecting global services, triaging bug reports and operator-driven feature requests Technical ownership of the deployment and day-to-day operation of SKAO-owned SRCNet services: monitoring and managing the services, maintaining the Kubernetes platform layer, responding to and diagnosing incidents and coordinating resolutions to ensure stability Manage service lifecycle and upgrades: plan and execute upgrades of platform components and deployed services Improve deployment and release processes: maintain CI/CD and GitOps workflows to support deployment and improve the team’s release management processes. Drive operational excellence and security practices: improve observability, documentation and security practices across SRCNet services. Mandatory Knowledge, Skills and Experience Experience working in a professional DevOps engineering capacity for at least two years Postgraduate qualification in Astronomy, Physics, Computer Science or a related and relevant field Proficiency in a modern programming language (e.g. Python) and familiarity with software engineering practices including version control, TDD and CI/CD pipelines, as well as infrastructure automation and GitOps-based deployment workflows (e.g. Helm, ArgoCD, Terraform or Ansible). Experience with Kubernetes and containerisation technologies (e.g. Docker, Singularity) in cloud or distributed infrastructure environments, including deployment, configuration and lifecycle management of containerised services. Demonstrable ability to diagnose and resolve complex operational issues across application, infrastructure and networking layers, supported by experience with observability and operational tooling (e.g. Prometheus, Grafana, Elastic stack), and the ability to manage workloads and targets in a dynamic and collaborative environment. Experience of building effective working relationships with engineers and scientists from a variety of cultures, to communicate ideas well and to foster a collaborative ethos. Experience with, or a proven commitment to, Agile practices, including the importance of customer focus and a pragmatic approach to decision making Desirable Knowledge, Skills and Experience Experience with database administration (we use a range of SQL and noSQL DBs) Background in scientific computing, data-intensive systems or research infrastructure. Experience implementing security practices such as vulnerability scanning, secrets management or access control in cloud-native environments. Experience with data management systems used in large-scale research environments. Experience with Agile/Scrum methodologies Equality Diversity and Inclusion Statement SKA Observatory recognises that our diversity is a strength. We aim to create a welcoming and inclusive environment where everyone feels they belong, and diverse perspectives and ideas thrive. As such, Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion are at the core of SKA Observatory’s agenda. Our aim is to recruit and retain the most talented individuals, regardless of gender, race, disability, age, sexual orientation, marital status, religion, nationality or background. Women have traditionally been under-represented in the fields of science and engineering; SKA Observatory welcomes and encourages female applicants. Where applicants with a disability need facilities or adjustments to enable them to participate in the recruitment process, these will be provided. SKA Observatory welcome all candidates, especially those from member countries. The “How to Apply” information contained within the SKA Observatory recruitment portal provides more detail regarding our application and selection approach.
